# Codex Security

Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
`@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK.

- **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md).
- **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start).
- **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or
  [GitHub Action](#github-actions).

## Features

- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
  your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. [Scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md).
- Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. [Integration workflows](docs/plugin-connectors.md).
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
  containers.

## Use in Codex

Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:

> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source
evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an
existing fix. See the [agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) for setup,
task selection, and recovery.

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+.
Python 3.10 also requires `tomli`.

Install the CLI globally and sign in:

```bash
npm install --global @openai/codex-security
cs login
```

Run your first scan from the repository directory:

```bash
cs scan .
```

When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the **REPORT** path in the
terminal. Run `cs scans show` from the same repository to find its latest
completed scan again. See [scan scope and follow-up work](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#understand-scan-scope-and-follow-up-work)
for how to interpret exclusions in the report.

`cs` and `codex-security` run the same CLI. If the short name conflicts with
another command, use `codex-security`. To skip the global install, or if npm
reports an `EEXIST` conflict, use `npx @openai/codex-security` in place of
`cs` for both login and scanning.

For CI, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` in the scan process's environment.
For a headless machine, see [device or SSH login](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#authentication).

### Scan options

Choose a scope and scan mode:

```bash
# Scan selected paths.
cs scan . --path src --path tests

# Scan committed changes from a base revision to HEAD.
cs scan . --diff origin/main

# Run a deep scan of the repository.
cs scan . --mode deep
```

Use `cs scan . --max-time 15` for an advisory 15-minute Standard investigation
allowance. See [investigation time](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#set-investigation-time)
for timing semantics and Deep Scan limits.

Use `cs --help` to browse commands, or `cs scan --help`
for scan options, cost limits, and patching after a scan.

For an application spread across repositories, see
[review one system across repositories](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#review-one-system-across-repositories).
Use [bulk scans](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#bulk-scans) for independent repository
reviews in one resumable campaign.

Scans use existing root and component `SECURITY.md` guidance. To write or
revise it, see [Generate SECURITY.md](#generate-securitymd).

Some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require
[Trusted Access for Cyber](https://chatgpt.com/cyber). For accounts with Daybreak
access, see [Daybreak opt-in](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#daybreak-opt-in) for the
Codex toggle and [Cyber access programs](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#select-a-cyber-access-program)
to select a program explicitly.

## TypeScript SDK

Install the package locally in your TypeScript project:

```bash
npm install @openai/codex-security
```

Then import it:

```ts
import { CodexSecurity } from "@openai/codex-security";

const security = new CodexSecurity();

try {
  const result = await security.run("/path/to/repository");
  console.log(result.reportPath);
} finally {
  await security.close();
}
```

The [SDK guide](sdk/typescript/docs/sdk.md) includes deep-scan configuration,
validation, severity classification, owner suggestions, and result handling.

Linked Git worktrees share scan history and saved findings when they use the same
Codex Security state directory. Keep `CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR` stable to retain
that shared history and sign-in scope. See the [scan history guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#scan-history-and-reruns).

## Read existing Cloud findings

When Codex Security Cloud is available to your account, the Security plugin's
`$cloud-findings` skill can read findings, reports, recorded assignment and
verification, and scan status in Codex desktop or the Codex CLI. Cloud is an
optional connection; local scans work without it.

See [Cloud connection setup and CLI reads](sdk/typescript/docs/sdk.md#read-existing-cloud-findings)
for authentication requirements and a read-only example.

## Generate SECURITY.md

Use `policy` to draft a new `SECURITY.md` or update an existing one. Use `--path`
to select a component:

```bash
cs policy .
cs policy . --path services/api --knowledge-base architecture.md
```

The command saves its draft outside the repository and leaves existing files
unchanged. Review the diff and notes, edit the draft, then copy only `SECURITY.md`
to the displayed **Policy target**. Keep the saved architecture and threat-model
documents outside the repository.

Scans already use root and component `SECURITY.md` files. Keep your current policy
if it needs no changes. When updating it, preserve its vulnerability-reporting
instructions. If the command says the policy is already up to date, no copy is
needed.

Files at `.github/SECURITY.md` or `docs/SECURITY.md` often contain reporting
instructions. Preserve them when drafting a policy; those locations do not
automatically provide repository-wide scan guidance. See the
[policy guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#generate-a-security-policy) for policy
locations, unanswered questions, saved artifacts, and SDK usage.

## Save and export threat models

Scans and policy generation save threat models with their results. Export a saved
model without starting another analysis:

```bash
cs export --scan SCAN_ID --artifact threat-model --output threatmodel.md
```

Omit `--scan` to use the current repository's latest completed scan. The
[export guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#exports-and-ci) also covers findings,
SARIF output for CI, and the offline TypeScript API. For ServiceNow Application
Vulnerability Response, see [Export findings for ServiceNow](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#export-findings-for-servicenow).

## GitHub Actions

To run a weekly repository scan on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu:

1. Add an OpenAI API key as the repository secret `CODEX_SECURITY_API_KEY`.
2. Copy the [weekly workflow](github-action/examples/repository.yml) to
   `.github/workflows/codex-security.yml`. Replace `REPLACE_WITH_REVIEWED_COMMIT`
   with the reviewed distribution commit SHA from an Action release.
3. To try the workflow before the next scheduled run, open **Actions → Codex
   Security repository → Run workflow**.

The example uses an estimated $5 limit per scan and reports findings without
failing the job. Requests in progress can exceed the limit. For a severity
threshold, pull request checks, or runner requirements, see the
[Action guide](github-action/README.md). For eligible accounts, see
[Daybreak access](github-action/README.md#daybreak-access-and-refusals).

## Containerized bulk scans

Scan a list of repositories with the included Docker Compose configuration,
which keeps results and authentication between runs. See the
[container quick start](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#containerized-bulk-scans).
The [workflow runner](docker/README.md#workflow-runner) runs individual CLI stages
in containers and can connect to a separately deployed findings service.

## Findings storage and deduplication

The [findings guide](sdk/typescript/docs/findings-service.md) covers local
storage, deduplication, and compatibility with independently operated endpoints
through `publish scan --to custom` and explicit `--findings-url`. The local
`serve` command and browser dashboard have been removed; existing databases and
scan artifacts remain available.

## Other providers

Scans support OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, and Cheaper Inference. Bedrock uses
AWS credentials and does not require a separate OpenAI login. See
[Bedrock setup](docs/bedrock.md) for AWS profiles, regions, and model access.

For OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, and Cheaper Inference, set the provider's API key and choose a supported
model. See [provider configuration](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#native-command-authentication-and-other-providers)
for examples.

## Documentation

- [Online documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/security/cli)
- [Agent workflows and recovery](docs/agent-workflows.md)
- [CLI reference](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md)
- [Imported finding identity and evidence](docs/scanner-imports/schema-guide.md)
- [Project configuration](docs/project-configuration.md)
- [Examples](examples/README.md)

To report a vulnerability privately, follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md).

<!-- codex-security-release-summary:start -->

<!-- release-section: highlights:start -->

## Highlights

Codex Security 0.10.0 gives clearer guidance when a patch is blocked, lets interrupted Standard scans resume, and adds a budget for batch scans.

- **Blocked patch results.** The patch prompt asks whether any files changed, what stopped the fix, and what to do next. When a fix depends on work outside the checkout, the result explains why the external change is needed and where it belongs when known. [#2609](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2609)
- **Standard scan setup.** Standard scans start with the vulnerability audit and load host-specific instructions when needed. Focused investigators receive their own briefs, and scan history records the file count from the scan's inventory. [#2046](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2046)
- **Resume interrupted Standard scans.** Run `codex-security scans resume SCAN_ID` to continue from a saved checkpoint in the original Codex session. The resumed scan retains its usage and budget. [#2610](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2610)
- **Batch scan budgets.** Set `--max-total-cost` on bulk or component scans to share one estimated budget across repositories or components, including retries and recoveries. In-flight work can exceed the estimate. [#2592](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2592)
- **Scanner imports and publication.** Import saved ArmorCode SAST findings into the local workbench. SDK callers can publish selected workbench finding versions to Cloud using retained evidence. [#2608](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2608) · [#2603](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2603)
- **Hosted remediation.** A hosted patch or verification that ends at a different commit reports `revision_changed` and retains its execution receipt. Retry from the requested revision. [#2583](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2583)

<!-- release-section: highlights:end -->

<!-- release-section: upgrades:start -->

## Upgrade notes

- **POSIX paths through symlinks.** Paths such as `link/../repo` now follow filesystem traversal. To resume an older bulk campaign whose source was normalized differently, enter its exact saved source path in the CSV. Use a new output directory to scan the corrected physical target. [#1709](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/1709)
- **MCP registration scripts.** Pass `--all` if you relied on selecting all clients after automatic detection found none, or pass `--agent NAME` for one client. Use `--package NAME` for bare npm package names previously passed to `--command`. [#2591](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2591)
- **Archived scanner captures and Cloud retries.** Recollect Semgrep Platform v1 and Snyk REST v1 captures with the current collectors. Finish interrupted Cloud submissions with the client that created them. If the outcome is uncertain, check the inbox job or repository records before submitting again. [#2602](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2602)
- **Patch follow-ups with scan budgets.** Run patch preparation separately when a scan has a cost limit. The scan rejects an explicit patch follow-up and skips its interactive patch offer. [#2592](https://github.com/openai/codex-security/pull/2592)

<!-- release-section: upgrades:end -->
<!-- codex-security-release-summary:end -->

# Agent Skills **Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.** Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`. Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps. Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on. --- ## Quick Start **Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more): ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # install all 25 skills npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list # browse before installing ``` Or grab individual skills: ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality # five-axis review before merge npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me # requirements interrogation, one question at a time npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development # red-green-refactor, enforced ``` > **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only > `skills//`, not the repo-level `references/` directory. The skill still > works, but paths to supplementary shared checklists are unavailable. Use a > whole-repo integration, clone the repository, or copy the needed checklist into > a `references/` directory inside the installed skill. This portability gap is > tracked in [#361](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/issues/361). Prefer a native integration? Pick your tool below.
Claude Code (recommended) **Marketplace install:** ``` /plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills ``` > **SSH errors?** The marketplace clones repos via SSH. If you don't have SSH keys set up on GitHub, either [add your SSH key](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account) or use the full HTTPS URL to force HTTPS cloning during the marketplace-add step: > ```bash > /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git > /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills > ``` > > If `/plugin install` still fails with `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` on Windows or macOS, the recommended workaround is to configure Git once to rewrite GitHub SSH URLs to HTTPS for subprocess clones: > ```bash > git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com: > ``` **Local / development:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git claude --plugin-dir /path/to/agent-skills ```
Cursor Put workflow skills under `.cursor/skills/` (sync from `agent-skills/skills/`) and short policies in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` — do not paste full skills into rules. Both directories live in your project; this repo does not ship a `.cursor/` folder. See [docs/cursor-setup.md](docs/cursor-setup.md).
Antigravity CLI Install as a native plugin for skills and subagents. In affected Antigravity CLI releases, legacy command TOMLs are reported as converted but their wrapper commands are not discoverable; invoke the underlying namespaced skills directly. See [docs/antigravity-setup.md](docs/antigravity-setup.md#lifecycle-workflows-and-command-compatibility). **Install from the repo:** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git agy plugin install ./agent-skills ```
Gemini CLI Install as native skills for auto-discovery, or add to `GEMINI.md` for persistent context. See [docs/gemini-cli-setup.md](docs/gemini-cli-setup.md). **Install from the repo:** ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git --path skills ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash gemini skills install ./agent-skills/skills/ ```
Windsurf Add skill contents to your Windsurf rules configuration. See [docs/windsurf-setup.md](docs/windsurf-setup.md).

release.name: Agent Skills 0.6.15
release.body:
Agent Skills 0.6.15 stops the security skill's staged-secret check from printing the secret it finds, fixes two simplify-ignore bugs that could corrupt protected code, and makes the constraints skill's security and accessibility gates actually fail CI.

## Security

- **The staged-secret check no longer echoes credentials** (#718, @santhiprakash, reported by @xmxxc in #717). The old `git diff --cached | grep` printed every matching line, so a staged key landed in the terminal and in any agent's transcript. It also read as clean when git failed. The check is now `git diff --cached -i -G'…' --name-only`: it prints only file names, and a git failure exits non-zero by itself. Fixed in all three places it was documented.

## Hooks

- **simplify-ignore restores re-indented placeholders cleanly** (#766, @Quinnod345, #765). If `/code-simplify` un-indented a placeholder or edited its reason, Stop wrote back a broken comment around the block, a syntax error in any `/* */` language. Blocks marked with `-- simplify-ignore-start` (SQL, Lua, Haskell) no longer warn that they were deleted, and a missing lock directory no longer stops Stop before every file is restored.

## Skills

- **Quality gates that fail when they should** (#694, @mavericksea-ai, #693). Semgrep and axe exit 0 even with blocking findings, so the constraints skill's examples could pass CI while breaking the written bar. The skill now ships a small report gate that blocks high and critical findings, and it says to run each enforced command against a deliberate violation before calling it enforced.
- **Contrast thresholds corrected** (#733, @CybotTM): large text is 18pt (24px) or 14pt bold, not 18px.
- One-line gotchas from @CybotTM: compact well before the host's context limit, which varies by host (#739); keep a contradicting caller or guard in the doubt review unit (#754); and an injected exception isn't a crash, and a mocked transaction isn't a rollback (#750).
- git-workflow-and-versioning fires on a pasted diff (#758), and security-and-hardening names session cookies in its description (#759), both @ayobamiseun as part of #620.
- The shipping error boundary types its `children` prop (#683, @rudycelekli).

## Evals

- `--eval <id>` runs a single behavioral case (#742, @CybotTM).
- The runner names any positive prompt that passes `top_k` without ranking first (#760), and the plugin-eval graders no longer expect command names that #714 removed, with the re-run recorded (#756), both @ayobamiseun.

## Thanks

Thanks to everyone who contributed and reviewed this release: @santhiprakash, @xmxxc, @Quinnod345, @mavericksea-ai, @CybotTM, @ayobamiseun, @rudycelekli and @federicobartoli.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/compare/0.6.14...0.6.15

# Astryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now:
by people and the agents working alongside them. **Currently in Beta** · Built on [React 19+](https://react.dev) and [StyleX](https://stylexjs.com) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@astryxdesign/core?label=npm&color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@astryxdesign/core) [![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@astryxdesign/core?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-astryx.atmeta.com-6741d9?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com) [![Storybook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Storybook-live-ff4785?logo=storybook&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/) [![Sandbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox-playground-A9792B)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/) **[Docs](https://astryx.atmeta.com)** · **[Storybook](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)** · **[Sandbox](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)** · **[Contributing](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)** · **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**
## Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. **What makes Astryx different:** - **Open internals.** Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. - **No styling lock-in.** Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with `className` using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. - **Customize without wrapping.** A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. - **Built for people and agents.** The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. ## Getting Started Astryx requires **React 19** or later (`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies of `@astryxdesign/core`). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: ```bash # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli ``` You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so `astryx` works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: ```bash npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli ``` Project install, global install, or both? `astryx docs global/project-global-or-both` compares them (both is recommended), and `astryx docs global` explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the **[@astryxdesign/core README](packages/core/README.md#quick-start)** for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your `package.json`: ```json "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } ``` Then use it as `npm run astryx -- component --list`. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. ## Packages | Package | Description | README | | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | [`@astryxdesign/core`](packages/core) | Components, theme system, and utilities | [README](packages/core/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/cli`](packages/cli) | CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods | [README](packages/cli/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/build`](packages/build) | Build plugins for StyleX source builds | [README](packages/build/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/theme-*`](packages/themes) | Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) | [README](packages/themes) | > `@astryxdesign/lab` (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. `@astryxdesign/vega` (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and `@astryxdesign/charts` (chart components) are published to npm only under the `@canary` dist-tag — there is no stable release yet. ## Principles These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it. - **Guidance over enforcement.** Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it. - **Strong, documented conventions.** Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves. - **One system for humans and AI.** The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too. - **Earned by measurement.** We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong. ## Architecture ### Foundations The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility. ### Components A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support. ### Patterns Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows. ## Project Structure | Directory | Purpose | | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `apps/` | Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook | | `packages/` | Published packages: core, cli, build, themes | | `internal/` | Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests | ## Contributing We welcome contributions! See **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)** for the full guide. Questions, or want a hand with a PR? Come find us in **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**. Our conventions and review rubrics live in the [Contributing wiki](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) — including [API Conventions](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/API-Conventions), [Design Conventions](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Design-Conventions), the [Component Lifecycle](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Component-Lifecycle), the [Contributing Templates](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing-Templates), and the [Blog Review Rubric](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Blog-Review-Rubric#three-required-scored-criteria). Read the relevant rubric before opening a PR. Quick start for contributors: this repo uses **Node 22+ on an active LTS line** and **pnpm 11**. Install pnpm directly, or enable [Corepack](https://nodejs.org/api/corepack.html) once so the pinned pnpm version installs automatically: ```bash corepack enable pnpm install ``` If `corepack` is missing, install pnpm directly or install Corepack manually; see the troubleshooting notes in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#troubleshooting). The Theme Showcase DOM tests use the root `ui` project for shared DOM and StyleX test setup. Run `pnpm exec vitest run --project ui apps/docsite/src/__tests__/theme-showcase/` from the repository root. ## License MIT

release.body:
Astryx 0.7.14 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.13  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.14 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.14  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.14
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- ComplexSelector: `disabledMessage` explains why a disabled selector is disabled. With `isDisabled`, a tooltip shows the reason on hover and keyboard focus, and the reason describes the trigger through `aria-describedby`. The disabled trigger keeps its tab stop, and pointer, keyboard and the imperative handle still cannot open the popup. With `renderTrigger`, the caller owns the control, and `disabledMessage` works with it too: the tooltip and the description go to that control. Drop the control's own tooltip while the selector is disabled, for example `tooltip={isDisabled ? undefined : 'Filter'}`, so it never shows two. Separately, a caller's own `aria-disabled` now reaches an enabled built-in trigger. (#5984)

- An anchored layer's entrance now slides from, and scales about, the side the layer lands on. Before, a layer that flipped because its requested side had no room still slid from that requested side, onto its trigger. The entrance also scales about the point where the layer meets its trigger, not the center of its box. A Selector list that opens over its selected item scales about the trigger's center and does not slide. This applies to Popover, DropdownMenu and its submenus, ContextMenu, Selector, ComplexSelector, Tooltip, HoverCard, Breadcrumbs and PowerSearch menus, and any layer that uses the shared entrance. Built-in layers have no option that keeps the old entrance. The public `layerAnimations` styles now also set `transform-origin`; a caller's own `transformOrigin` listed after them still wins. (#10771)

- `useMenuPress` with no `longPressDelayMs` now follows DropdownMenu's finger rules on every device: a finger or a pen opens the menu as it presses (inside a scroll view, once the 150 ms content-touch delay has passed), and the finger that opened it picks a row only after moving 10 px. To keep the previous behavior, a 500 ms hold and a pick at the opening finger's lift, pass `longPressDelayMs: 500`. (#8078)

- Under a finger or a pen, on every device, the trigger of an anchored DropdownMenu or MoreMenu now opens its menu as it is pressed, instead of after a 500 ms hold. Inside a scroll view it opens once the 150 ms content-touch delay has passed with no scroll, so a scroll that starts on it still scrolls. To keep the previous behavior, a tap that opens at the lift and a 500 ms hold, pass `presentation="popover"`. A menu shown as a bottom sheet, and a mouse, are unchanged. (#8078)

- SegmentedControl: a drag that drifts off the control keeps choosing by its horizontal position, clamped to the end segments, and the lift commits that segment. A mouse or a pen drags the same way. Escape or a browser cancel takes the press back, and the highlight returns at once. (#10978)

- Tokenizer is now an InputGroup-compatible control (#3520). Inside an `InputGroup` it consumes `InputGroupContext` instead of rendering its own `Field`, so the group owns the single label, description, and status chrome — no more duplicated label or nested field wrapper. The typeahead input is named by the group label plus the Tokenizer's own label (composed with `getInputARIA`, so `aria-describedby` merges the group's description/status with the input-local disabled reason rather than replacing it), and the control adopts the shared `groupStyles.inGroup` border/radius treatment so it joins the group's seam. The group also owns size, the disabled state, and validation: a disabled group disables its Tokenizer, a grouped Tokenizer takes the group's `size` (an explicit larger `size` no longer escapes the row), and its local `description`/`status` are neither referenced from `aria-describedby` nor painted beside the group's status. Because the group is a fixed-height single-line surface, a grouped Tokenizer keeps its tokens on one scrolling row instead of wrapping past the shared border — cap selections with `maxEntries` or summarize them with `tokenOverflowBehavior`. Its end controls (the clear button, `endContent`, and the busy indicator) hold the end of that row: tokens scroll beside them, never underneath. The row hides its native scrollbar and fades whichever edge hides tokens instead; forced colors bring back a thin native scrollbar. Keyboard users reach hidden tokens through their remove buttons (Shift+Tab from the input), and a disabled Tokenizer's row becomes its own Tab stop while it overflows, named by the Tokenizer's label, so the arrow keys can scroll it. (#4405)

- TimeInput, DateTimeInput: under a finger, the bottom sheet's minute wheel loops, as UIDatePicker's does: past 59 comes 00, and the hour stays, as on iOS. A drag, a fling, a tap or an arrow key passes the seam. Home, End and a click on a minute never pass it. The hour wheel does not loop yet. Each minute is still listed once for assistive technology. (#10953)

### Fixes

- When a page mounts both the package's AppShell and a swizzled AppShell as outermost shells, only the first now keeps the fixed main-region id; the other takes a generated id, as two package shells already did. Before, each copy kept its own claim list, so both shells used `astryx-app-shell-main` and the page had a duplicate id. No API changes. (#11208)

- BottomSheet: a finger's pull down on the sheet's content is handled by the sheet's touch listeners alone, and it releases at the speed of the whole pull. Before, the content's pointer handlers, which serve a mouse or a pen, began the same drag first and took pointer capture, and the capture change cancelled that drag one move later. The touch listeners then began the drag again, or, in Chromium, the content's own pan could start under it. The release speed counted only the moves after the drag began, so a fast flick on the content that the page received as two or three moves read as no speed and sprang back, where the same flick on the grab handle closed the sheet. A flick on the content now closes the sheet as a flick on the grab handle does. This also applies to the sheets that Tokenizer and PowerSearch open. A mouse or pen pull from the content also releases at the speed of the whole pull. No release threshold changes. (#11145)

- BottomSheet: a move of a touch drag no longer restyles the sheet's content. Each move writes the scrim's opacity on the dialog as a custom property, and the property inherited into the sheet, so the browser restyled every element in the sheet on every move: 51 elements a move in a Tall sheet with a short list, 84 in PowerSearch's Filters sheet with three filters, and more with more content. The sheet's panel now ends that inheritance, and a move restyles the dialog, its backdrop, the panel and the edge tint. The scrim follows the drag as before. This applies to the sheet that owns the scrim: a single BottomSheet, or the first sheet of a stack, such as PowerSearch's Filters sheet and Tokenizer's sheet. (#11154)

- BottomSheet: in Safari, and in every browser on iPhone and iPad, a swipe on the sheet's content that starts slowly now moves the sheet, so a slow swipe down can close it. Before, on content that fits, when the finger's first move was 8 px or less, in either direction, the sheet stopped answering that swipe: it stayed open, or moved a few pixels and fell back. Fast swipes and swipes on the grab bar already worked, and Chromium browsers were not affected. The fix applies wherever the touched content has nothing to scroll: a sheet whose content fits, and the fixed header or footer around a list. That includes the PowerSearch and Tokenizer sheets. At the top of a list that scrolls, a pull down now also moves the sheet when the finger first wobbles up by less than 5 px; a move up of 5 px or more still scrolls the list. In every browser, the sheet now decides who owns a touch on its content once, at the first move past 8 px. A mostly vertical pull at a scroll edge is the sheet's. A mostly sideways move, such as a swipe along a row of chips, is not the sheet's for the rest of that touch. Before, at the top of a list, a sideways swipe that drifted more than 8 px down, or a pull that began more sideways than down, also moved the sheet. (#11140)

- Button: a disabled or loading submit or reset Button, including one in a disabled ButtonGroup or InputGroup, no longer submits or resets its form when clicked in server-rendered HTML before the page hydrates or when JavaScript fails to load. It renders as a plain button until hydration, then takes its own type again, with no change to what people see or hear. (#11107)

- A Carousel's scroll buttons no longer cover the scroller's keyboard focus ring. Each button now sits just inside the ring instead of straddling the carousel's edge, so the whole ring stays visible while the scroller has focus (#10722). (#10726)

- A transient copy that carries an animation still waiting for its first frame now runs it in step with the original. On a busy page, the SideNav rail's leaving copy could start the toggle's press fade a frame or more after the toggle's own. (#10983)

- `CommandPalette`: refresh results when its `searchSource` changes while it is open. (#9679)

- createISOTimeString answers null unless the trimmed string is H:M or H:M:S with one or two digits per field (a seconds fraction is still accepted and dropped), instead of reading "2:30 PM" as 02:30 (12 hours off) and "14:30abc" as 14:30 (#11023)

- FileInput's dropzone shows its status message below the drop area by default, so it no longer covers the drop area; an explicit `statusVariant="attached"` still renders as before. (#11195)

- A pan over the page that the browser doesn't take as a scroll no longer closes an open popover or selector list, and no longer taps the page element under the finger. (#11038)

- A swizzled overlay and the package's components now share one set of focus regions and one mobile keyboard model: nested focus regions from the package and a copy no longer both answer the same Tab, and package and copied fields agree on the keyboard's height, its layout guide and which elements ride it. No API changes. (#10831)

- On a phone, a press on a control at rest no longer measures the page, so a scroll that starts there does not wait. Hit areas no longer measure while the page scrolls or while a parent's animation moves them, such as a screen that slides in. A press on a control that a parent moves still measures the page. When a parent starts to move after the last measurement, the browser's own hit test decides the tap. No API changes. (#11083)

- The arrow-key hint that Toolbar, TabList and SegmentedControl show on first keyboard focus now stays until you press an arrow key or Escape, or move focus out of the group (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus). It used to disappear after 3 seconds, sometimes before it could be read, and Escape did not close it. Escape now closes only the hint, through the shared layer dismissal stack, and keeps focus where it is. `useKeyboardHint`'s `dismissAfterMs` no longer defaults to 3000; leave it unset. (#10564)

- Closing a Lightbox stops a video that was playing. The viewer stays mounted, so the picture and its sound would otherwise continue after Close, Escape, or a tap outside. A viewer that is already closed does not start playback either. Opening it again plays the current video when `hasAutoPlay` is set. A video inside the caption stays stopped. (#10692)

- A swizzled ListItem inside the package's List (or a package ListItem inside a swizzled List) now leaves the way a package row does: it keeps what it showed on screen, such as a swipe's travel, for its exit. Before, the List and the ListItem kept separate records of the

Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](charts/openbot/README.md) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, cluster sizing, or an existing Intelligence deployment, use the [full Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and [the Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). The guide covers cloud-specific values, storage, secrets, sign-in, networking, upgrades, and troubleshooting. Use the evaluation below only through a local port-forward; configure sign-in and TLS before sharing a deployment. 1. **Get the source.** Skip this if you already have a checkout. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` 2. **Create `openbot-secrets.yaml` locally.** Replace the placeholders with your license and model key. Keep this file out of source control. ```yaml secrets: licenseToken: "" modelApiKey: "" ``` 3. **Install.** ```sh helm dependency build charts/openbot helm install openbot charts/openbot \ --namespace openbot --create-namespace \ --values charts/openbot/ci/vanilla-values.yaml \ --values openbot-secrets.yaml \ --timeout 15m ``` 4. **Open your evaluation.** ```sh kubectl -n openbot get pods,jobs kubectl -n openbot port-forward svc/openbot-server 3001:3001 ``` Open . This configuration is single-user: anyone who can reach it is an administrator. Keep the port-forward local. The chart creates the runtime credentials, installs the databases, bootstraps Intelligence, and sets up the Learning container and scheduled jobs. Automatic Learning uses your model key too. For a team deployment, follow the [Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md) to configure authentication, TLS, your database, secrets, persistent storage, and network policies. For a single-container alternative, see [Deploy it](#deploy-it). ## Run from source Use the template to customize the workspace, branding, Bots, and skills. The source setup below uses managed Intelligence by default; [local Intelligence](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) is also available. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` ### Requirements To run the open-source template locally, you’ll need the following. - Docker, for PostgreSQL and the shipped Bots. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4+, for the app, the API server and the tests (some tests fail on 1.3). - A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license. A free plan is available, and Intelligence can be self-hosted. - A model key. The proof-of-concept Bot uses OpenAI; the LangGraph Bot can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. ### Quick start The example configuration sets `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, so you can try the app as a local administrator. Configure [sign-in](#sign-in) before giving anyone else access. On a Mac, the free Developer plan also covers [running Intelligence locally](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) with Docker. > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Paste [`prompt.txt`](prompt.txt) into it first. It carries the > same steps as below plus the things that are easy to get wrong: which of the blank keys in > `.env.example` are actually yours to fill (the CopilotKit key and a model key), which the start > script fills for you, and what each start-up refusal means. Every claim in it is checked against > this repository. 1. Create `.env`: ```sh cp .env.example .env bun install ``` 2. Connect a fresh managed Intelligence project: ```sh npx --yes copilotkit@latest login npx --yes copilotkit@latest project select bun scripts/setup-learning.ts ``` The helper provisions the selected project's runtime key, creates or reuses its `openbot` Learning container, then writes both settings to `.env`. It preserves custom container assignments and never replaces an existing OpenBot key; with one set, it only creates `openbot` in that key's project if it is missing. For fresh self-hosted setup, set `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL` to that deployment's HTTPS API origin (or `http://localhost` for a local one) and run the helper without the two `npx` commands. It opens an isolated Chrome or Edge window for your usual sign-in and project choice; install either browser first. For CLI-managed local evaluation installs, it discovers the matching dashboard with the newest installed or cached CopilotKit CLI and uses that dashboard for login and session requests. Discovery runs offline with Bun, without downloading the CLI or requiring `npx` on your PATH. If no CLI is available, manually hosted deployments use their API origin for sign-in. Complete the local auth approval shown in the browser when prompted. The runtime API URL stays unchanged. It writes the API URL, the key and the container, not `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL`, so set that one to the same deployment yourself. Once `openbot` exists, the server assigns it as the default by itself unless [Admin → Automatic Learning](docs/automatic-learning.md) has a saved setting. Managed Intelligence needs no separate license token. The same CopilotKit CLI sign-in provisions Composio automatically when you run `bash scripts/start.sh`. If that cannot complete, OpenBot still starts, with apps unavailable. You can run `bun run setup:composio` first to prepare it separately, or later to retry; it does not need a Learning container. The helper creates or reuses one isolated Composio project for this installation and saves its project key to `.env`. Existing Composio keys and Arcade configurations are preserved. Keep the private `.env.openbot-installation-id` file across restarts and interrupted setup attempts; do not copy it into a new installation. This needs a published CopilotKit CLI with `integrations composio provision` and the hosted provisioning service enabled. See [Composio setup](docs/plugins/composio.md#automatic-project-setup) for deployment preparation. 3. Fill the remaining required values: - `OPENAI_API_KEY` Keep the managed Intelligence URLs from `.env.example` unless you run Intelligence yourself. The example `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is public and fine locally; generate your own with: ```sh openssl rand -base64 32 ``` 4. Run: ```sh bash scripts/start.sh ``` 5. Open . `scripts/start.sh` starts Docker services, applies migrations, starts the API server on port 3001, starts the routine worker, starts the app on port 3010, and checks that the services answer their own health routes before printing next steps. `scripts/stop.sh` takes the same things down, including each Bot's computer, which compose does not own; `--keep-computers` leaves the computers running. Nothing is deleted: the database, the Bots' files and their browser profiles are volumes. ### On Windows Run the clone inside WSL 2 with Ubuntu, and run every step above from an Ubuntu terminal. [Windows (WSL 2)](docs/development.md#windows-wsl-2) lists what to install in Ubuntu first. Keep an Ubuntu terminal open while you use OpenBot, and open the app from your Windows browser at . ### Intelligence on your own machine To try Intelligence on one Mac instead of the managed service, follow [Evaluate Intelligence locally](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/self-hosting-local). The free [Developer plan](https://www.copilotkit.ai/pricing) qualifies. The local license lasts 30 days and `npx copilotkit@latest local renew` renews it as often as you need, while your account is in good standing. It is a preview for macOS with Docker Desktop, not a production installation. Run its `npx copilotkit@latest local connect` from the OpenBot root, where `.env` is. That command writes `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL`, `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL` and `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` to `.env`. OpenBot reads those settings directly; no key copying or renaming is needed. `INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` remains supported for older configurations. When both are set, the non-empty CLI key takes precedence so reconnecting uses the new project's key. To give the Bots a Learning container on that stack, see [Automatic Learning](docs/automatic-learning.md). ## Deploy it One image carries the app, the API, the browser the Bots drive, and optionally PostgreSQL. Same `.env`, no Kubernetes. ```sh # The published image. Nothing to clone and nothing to build. docker run -p 3001:3001 --env-file .env \ -e EMBEDDED_POSTGRES=on -v openbot-data:/var/lib/postgresql \ ghcr.io/copilotkit/openbot:latest # Or the tree you have in front of you. docker build -t openbot . docker run -p 3001:3001 --env-file .env \ -e EMBEDDED_POSTGRES=on -v openbot-data:/var/lib/postgresql openbot ``` Everything is on 3001 here, the app included, rather than the 3010 the clone uses. `latest` is the most recent release and a version tag such as `:v1.0.1` pins one. Leave `EMBEDDED_POSTGRES` off and set `DATABASE_URL` to point at a database you already run. [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md) has the minimum sizes, the platform notes, and how it behaves behind more than one replica. ## Try it Pick a task you know well enough to review. For example, ask a Bot to check a hotel receipt against a travel policy in Drive. Have it show the room rate and tax separately so you can decide whether the claim meets the nightly limit. Use **Teach a Bot** to record the steps you want it to follow on the next claim. - Open `/bot` and ask: `Open news.ycombinator.com and tell me the top story.` - Ask the Bot to fill out , then inspect `/admin/audit`. - Open `/admin/boundaries`, add a deny rule or preset, and retry the same browser action. - Create a Bot from `/bots`, give it a standing role, and start a channel with it. ## What it is In Personal Edition, you start with one assistant on your computer. With the source template, Docker Compose starts the supporting services, PostgreSQL stores the workspace configuration, and you choose the model. OpenBot encrypts stored model credentials and keeps them out of logs. The team template comes with two Bots. **General Assistant** helps with everyday work. **Knowledge** answers questions from the company documents you connect and cites its sources. **Before upgrading.** No migrations run in this release: the database stays at
`0088_approval_reviewer_guidance`, and a 1.0.1 database is used as it is. Upgrading from 1.0.0 or
0.3.x runs the migrations listed under 1.0.1, and a database that has run them does not go back:
restore the backup taken before the upgrade instead. Three things change for an existing OpenBot
Desktop installation:
- On Windows OpenBot now always runs in a Podman machine of its own, `openbot`, beside any of
  yours, and on a Mac it does when yours is rootless, after asking to pause it (below). An
  installation that ran in a machine of yours starts fresh in `openbot`, and its earlier data stays
  in your machine.
- At setup and at every Start, a Docker Desktop or Podman too old to run OpenBot is updated
  (below). Docker Desktop quits while it updates, which stops its containers; the ones that were
  running are started again afterwards.
- OpenBot Desktop's back end and the Helm chart move to CopilotKit Intelligence 0.16.0-rc.11, and
  the bundled CLI to `copilotkit@7bd073b` (below).

### OpenBot Desktop

- **Installing a new OpenBot over the old one on Windows never offers to delete your data, and
  uninstalling stops what OpenBot runs.** Running a new installer over an installed OpenBot opened
  the old version's uninstaller in the middle of the update, with a "Delete the application data"
  box, and one wrong tick deleted your Bots and conversations. The old version is now removed
  silently, as an update, on the Installing page, which says "Removing the previous version of
  OpenBot. Your Bots and data stay." with its progress bar moving. If OpenBot is open, the installer
  asks before it closes it. Uninstalling from Settings > Apps used to close OpenBot and leave its
  containers, its services and its Podman machine (`openbot`) running. It now stops them first,
  with the same Compose OpenBot runs, and never touches your own Podman machines or containers.
  Tick "Delete the application data" to remove OpenBot's machine, the backend OpenBot created and
  OpenBot's files in its installation folder as well, so installing again starts from nothing; a
  file of yours in that folder stays. Otherwise they stay, stopped, for a reinstall to find. And on
  Windows, an OpenBot whose own Podman machine is gone makes it again when it opens. It used to open
  on "OpenBot can't run on this computer as it's set up", having looked at your own machine.
- **Setup says what self-contained means up front, and asks about usage data last.** The first
  screen, "Set up OpenBot (self-contained)", says this version runs entirely on your computer,
  backend included, that setup takes between 1 and 10 minutes depending on your internet speed,
  and that in production OpenBot for Business runs on your own infrastructure with Kubernetes, or on
  OpenBot Cloud, with a link to book a demo. The usage-data notice moved off
  it to the foot of the last screen, Finishing setup, as a small checkbox, checked by default as
  before: it is the same setting as Settings > General > Privacy > Share usage data. The Account
  step's heading is now "Get your free license key".
- **OpenBot uses its own Podman machine when yours can't run it, and leaves yours as it is.** A
  Podman machine made with `podman machine init` is rootless, and OpenBot used it and stopped at
  "Change this computer's setup" because local Intelligence needs rootful Podman. On Windows even a
  rootful machine of yours left chat unable to reach OpenBot's back end. OpenBot now makes and uses
  its own rootful machine, `openbot`, as on a computer with none. On Windows it runs beside yours,
  which keeps running untouched, and never takes Docker's default pipe (`docker_engine`), so your
  Docker tools and Docker Desktop keep reaching what they did. On a Mac, where Podman runs one
  machine at a time, OpenBot asks before it pauses your rootless machine while it runs (**Pause my
  Podman**), and Quit starts yours again with its containers. Docker, and a rootful machine of
  yours on a Mac, are used as before. Your default Podman connection is never changed. An
  installation that ran in your own machine starts fresh in `openbot`; its old data stays in your
  machine.
- **OpenBot updates Docker Desktop or Podman when it is too old to run OpenBot.** A computer with
  Docker Desktop 4.27 got through setup and then stopped at Start with "Compose config exited with
  exit status: 15", an error nobody could act on. OpenBot now checks the engine at setup and at
  every Start, before Compose reads anything, and updates one that is too old for you: Docker
  Compose before 2.27.2 (Docker Desktop before 4.32), or Podman before 6.1. Docker Desktop's update
  comes from Docker's own update feed, is checked against Docker's checksums and signature, and
  installs over the one you have, keeping its images, containers and volumes; the containers that
  were running before are started again once it is back. Podman's is OpenBot's own pinned
  installer over the old one, and every Podman machine that was running before, yours included, is
  running afterwards with its containers. A Mac asks for your password, and an all-users Docker
  Desktop on Windows for Windows' approval. The row for what's installing in the background says
  why it is updating and shows the update's own lines in full, and the Account step waits for the
  update and says so. Where an update can't be done for you, such as a Mac or PC too old for the
  newest Docker Desktop, or an Intel Mac with an old Podman (Podman publishes its Mac package for
  Apple silicon only), one plain step says what to do. Separately, the Compose file now starts on
  an older Compose too: with no harness Bot picked, Compose 2.25 and older refused the whole
  project.
- **A Podman machine that stops answering is restarted.** A Podman machine OpenBot uses that had
  lost its Docker API failed setup and Start until you restarted it yourself, and Quit could not
  stop the back end, so the next launch said "OpenBot had trouble shutting down last time." At every
  check, including Start and Retry after a relaunch, and before Stop and Quit, such a machine is now
  stopped and started once, your default machine included. A failure while setup runs behind the
  Account step now has Try again.
- **Start says in the log what it is waiting on, and why it gave up.** A Start that waited five
  minutes for OpenBot's services and then said "OpenBot didn't get ready in time" left nothing in
  the log in between. Each wait now writes what it asked (the address or the back end's status),
  each new answer and the same one again once a minute, and why it ended, with how long it took and
  the last answer.
- **The big downloads start on the first screen, before you click Install.** Nothing used to
  download until Install, and then one thing at a time: on a new Mac, Podman, then the 937 MB
  engine image with no progress shown, then 1.1 GB of OpenBot's software. Now the engine image,
  Podman's installer, the deployment and, when Docker or Podman already runs, OpenBot's software
  start downloading as soon as the first screen shows, side by side, while you sign in and enter
  your Mac password. The first screen says how far they are ("Downloading OpenBot. About 3 minutes
  left.", with the bytes under a bar), and the row for what's installing in the background carries
  on with it. A download stopped by quitting carries on from where it stopped next time,
  and every file is checked against its pinned digest before it is used. Podman builds its machine
  from the downloaded image instead of fetching its own. With less free disk than OpenBot needs,
  the first screen says how much is free and how much is needed, and the downloads start once
  there is room. Nothing is installed before you are asked.
- **OpenBot's own software downloads on the first screen too, before there is anything to run it.**
  On a new Mac or PC, or with Docker Desktop not running, OpenBot's images (about 1.1 GB for the
  default Bot) waited for the engine to start, then downloaded behind it. They now download from
  the first screen with everything else, into the same cache, checked against their digests and
  carried on after a quit. Once the engine answers, Install loads them into it, so the step after
  it no longer downloads them. Anything that didn't download or load is downloaded then, as before.
- **An update downloads before you click Update.** As soon as a new version of OpenBot is out,
  OpenBot Desktop downloads what it runs in the background while you keep working: the parts for
  the Bots you use, and the back end's when it changes too, kept until you update. Clicking Update
  then stops OpenBot, backs it up, updates it and starts it again, with nothing big left to
  download. The update offer, Settings › This computer and the setup window say the new version
  "is downloading in the background (40%).", then that it "is ready to install. It takes a few
  minutes." It downloads one part at a time, waits while OpenBot starts, stops or updates, never
  stops or restarts anything you are using, and downloads nothing when the disk is short of room
  (the Desktop log says why, and the update downloads as before). Candidates and internal builds,
  which do not update themselves, download nothing ahead.
- **downloads.copilotkit.ai serves each release's `desktop-images.json`.** It answered 403, so the
  list of a release's images could only come from GitHub.
- **The Status window, Settings > This computer and the Install step say what's running in plain
  words.** The Status window, opened from the menu bar or the system tray, and Settings > This
  computer said "Back end", "Container engine", "Podman" or "Docker" and the build's commit and
  time. Both now name each part by what it does: App, OpenBot's services, and Software OpenBot runs
  on, with "App and Bots" for what was "Front end and Bots". They show the version on its own, and
  the engine, the build and Docker's container names stay in Copy diagnostics and the logs. A
  stopped app on This computer says it isn't using memory, where it said its memory couldn't be
  measured. On the Install step, the rest of OpenBot downloads alongside OpenBot's own download,
  and both said they were in progress at once ("Step 2 of 4" and "Step 3 of 4"). The step now shows
  one step at a time: the rest of OpenBot is step 3, shown once step 2 is done, as far along as it
  got meanwhile.
- **Windows setup no longer opens Microsoft's "Welcome to Windows Subsystem for Linux" window, and
  the installer asks plainly to close a running OpenBot.** The welcome window opened partway
  through setup, the first time OpenBot's Podman machine was made on a computer with no Linux
  distribution. It isn't OpenBot's and isn't needed, so OpenBot now marks it as already seen for
  you before it makes the machine. Installing over a running OpenBot said "OpenBot is running!
  Click OK to kill it". It now says "OpenBot is open. Click OK to close it and continue."
- **Setup on a new Windows computer waits for OpenBot's Podman machine's network, sets it up again
  when it doesn't come up, and asks for a Windows restart when only that fixes it.** On the first
  boot after Windows Subsystem for Linux was turned on, the machine's network could fail to come
  up. Accepting the license agreement stopped at "OpenBot couldn't prepare this computer to run it.
  Try again.", and Try again then failed the downloads, again and again, until Windows restarted.
  OpenBot now waits up to half a minute for the machine's network, checks it again before the
  downloads, and restarts its own machine once when it is still down, which sets the network up
  from scratch. A Podman machine of yours that shares that network is never stopped. If it is still
  down, setup shows "Restart Windows to finish", with Restart now, instead of Try again. OpenBot
  checks the network every time it op
